open_questions: Sector depth decreased 46.93% within same TESS-SPOC pipeline; spot-crossing vs baseline unocculted spots needs multi-color transit photometry or spectroscopic activity indices

Ultra-short 0.969-day period with duration ratio 1.742 (1.53 for Gaia radius) and fit_log_density_ratio -2.092, star_density_penalty 5603; unlikely for a true planet but also inconsistent with a synchronized binary density - needs RV mass and stable ephemeris test

Signal period 0.968957d equals stellar rotation 0.9664999999999999d (ratio 1.0025421624418003, amplitude 65116 ppm in sector 21 and 70975 ppm in sector 47); flare/variability chi2/dof 316.5; need activity diagnostics to show period coincidence is chance vs harmonic EB
dossier.public_summary: TESS finds a repeating 0.97-day flat-bottomed dip right on this young M dwarf, with no secondary eclipse and a size near a Neptunian planet even after correcting for Gaia radius. The dip looks planetary, but its depth halves between two sectors and its period matches the star’s own 0.97-day spot cycle almost exactly, so strong stellar activity and a very short duration remain to be checked with out-of-transit monitoring and spectroscopy.

reasons.why: Difference imaging puts the dip on the target in both sectors and rules out neighbours that could fake it; no plausible_within_1px source.
Strongly flat-bottomed, opposite to V-shaped binary/grazing signature which favors a transiting body.
Planet-sized despite depth change; Gaia radius 0.462-0.465 implies rp 6.61-6.65 Rearth, still below stellar >22.
High-SNR period reproduced over 49 transits by two independent pipeline apertures, not driven by few events.
Depth halved from sector 21 to 47 argues against a stable blended EB on target; consistent with spot-crossing on this active star as the main alternative remains planet.
